Anderson]]. Inspired by the 1990 novel ''[[Vineland]]'' by [[Thomas Pynchon]], the film's [[ensemble cast]] includes [[Leonardo DiCaprio]], [[Sean Penn]], [[Benicio del Toro]], [[Regina Hall]], [[Teyana Taylor]], and [[Chase Infiniti]], in her film debut. The film follows a drug-using washed-up former [[revolutionary]] who is thrust back into the conflict when an amoral tenacious [[counterterrorist]] agent resurfaces after sixteen years to bring them to justice to cover his past sins.

Anderson had wanted to adapt ''Vineland'' since the early 2000s, and eventually incorporated his own stories into the narrative while writing the screenplay. [[Principal photography]] took place in [[California]] from January to June 2024 using [[VistaVision]], becoming one of the first films to use the format since the 1960s. Following its premiere on September 8, 2025, ''One Battle After Another'' was released in the United States by [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] on September 26. With a budget of $130–175&nbsp;million, it is the most expensive film of Anderson's career and the highest-grossing at over $213&nbsp;million worldwide.

''One Battle After Another'' received acclaim and [[List of accolades received by One Battle After Another|numerous accolades]]. At the [[98th Academy Awards]], it was nominated for 13 awards and won [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] (Penn), [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]], [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Film Editing]], and the inaugural [[Academy Award for Achievement in Casting|Best Casting]] award. It also received one win from a record seven nominations at the [[32nd Actor Awards]]; three wins at the [[31st Critics' Choice Awards]], including [[Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]]; four wins at the [[83rd Golden Globes]], including [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy]]; and six wins at the [[79th British Academy Film Awards]], including [[BAFTA Award for Best Film|Best Film]]. The film was listed by the [[American Film Institute]] as one of the top ten films of 2025 and won five awards from the [[National Board of Review]], including [[National Board of Review Award for Best Film|Best Film]].

==Plot==
<!-- Per WP:FILMPLOT, plot summaries for feature films should be between 400 and 700 words. Please check the word count before making any additions. -->
"Ghetto" Pat Calhoun and Perfidia Beverly Hills are lovers and members of a [[Far-left politics|far-left]] militant revolutionary group, the French 75. While breaking out detained immigrants from [[Otay Mesa Detention Center]], Perfidia sexually humiliates the commanding officer, Steven J. Lockjaw, who afterward becomes obsessed with her. Later, when <!-- DO NOT CHANGE TO STEVEN! He's mainly referred to by his surname. -->Lockjaw catches Perfidia planting a bomb, he lets her go after she agrees to his demand to meet him for sex. Soon after, Perfidia becomes pregnant.

After Perfidia gives birth to a girl they name Charlene, Pat tries to persuade her to settle down, but she instead abandons Pat and Charlene to continue her revolutionary activities. Perfidia is arrested after murdering a security guard during a botched bank robbery. Lockjaw arranges for her to avoid prison in exchange for information on key French 75 members. Perfidia enters witness protection, while Lockjaw uses the information she provided to hunt down and [[Summary execution|summarily execute]] her comrades. French 75 member Howard Sommerville gives Pat and Charlene stolen identities as Bob and Willa Ferguson, while Perfidia flees witness protection for Mexico.

Sixteen years later, living off-the-grid in the [[sanctuary city]] of Baktan Cross, California, Bob has become a paranoid stoner. He is protective of Willa, now a teenager who resents Bob's substance abuse, and told her that her mother was a hero who died when she was a baby. Through his anti-immigration efforts, Lockjaw has become a [[Colonel (United States)|colonel]] and a prominent figure within the U.S. security agencies. When Lockjaw is invited to become a member of the Christmas Adventurers Club, a white supremacist secret society, he seeks to kill Willa to hide his past interracial relationship with Perfidia. Lockjaw sends [[bounty hunter]] Avanti Q to capture Howard, who is able to transmit a distress signal to the French 75 before he is forced to reveal Bob and Willa's location.

Using an immigration and drug enforcement operation as cover, Lockjaw sends troops to Baktan Cross. French 75 member Deandra rescues Willa before her school dance is raided and takes her to a convent of revolutionary nuns, where she is told the truth about her mother's betrayal. Bob is warned by the French 75 of Lockjaw's imminent arrival. Escaping through a hidden tunnel, Bob is helped by Sergio St. Carlos, Willa's karate sensei and a community leader, who also evacuates immigrants via a hidden passage. After learning about the convent from another French 75 member, Bob flees with Sergio's students across rooftops but falls and is arrested then hospitalized without being recognized.

The Christmas Adventurers club find evidence of Lockjaw's scandalous relationship with Perfidia, and that Willa may be his child. Using the euphemism “clean”, they send member Tim Smith to kill Lockjaw and Willa. By [[Mobile phone tracking|tracing her phone]], Lockjaw locates Willa at the convent, where Deandra is arrested. Holding Willa hostage, Lockjaw [[Genetic testing|tests their DNA]] in front of her, confirming she is his biological daughter. Sergio arranges Bob's escape and drives him to the convent. When they are pursued by the police, Sergio diverts the police so Bob can escape. Bob reaches the convent, and fails to snipe Lockjaw with Sergio's rifle. Lockjaw hires Avanti to kill Willa, but Avanti refuses due to her age; he agrees instead to deliver her to a far-right militia. 

Tim shoots Lockjaw as he is driving, causing Lockjaw to crash. While searching for Willa, Bob discovers Lockjaw's body at the crash site. Avanti brings Willa to the militia, but after a change of heart, frees her and is killed in a shootout with the militia. Willa escapes with Avanti's car and pistol with Tim in pursuit as Bob desperately tries to catch up. Willa lures Tim into a crash by exploiting a [[blind summit]], shooting and killing him when he fails to respond with the revolutionary countersign. Bob finds Willa, who demands the countersign. Bob is able to talk her down, and they embrace.

Some time later, a severely scarred Lockjaw is seemingly welcomed into the Christmas Adventurers Club, but they fatally gas then cremate him instead. Returning home with Willa, Bob gives her a letter from Perfidia, in which she apologizes for her actions and vows to someday reunite with her family. Later, Bob gives Willa his blessing as she departs for a protest in [[Oakland, California|Oakland]].

==Production==
===Development===
[[File:Paul Thomas Anderson in 2025.jpg|upright|thumb|Writer and director [[Paul Thomas Anderson]]]]

[[Paul Thomas Anderson]] had considered adapting the 1990 novel ''[[Vineland]]'' by [[Thomas Pynchon]] since the early 2000s, but struggled, believing his love for the novel would get in the way of his ability to fairly rework it.<ref name="Vineland">{{cite web |last=Pearce |first=Leonard |date=September 8, 2025 |title=Steven Spielberg Praises Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another': 'What an Insane Movie' |url=https://thefilmstage.com/steven-spielberg-praises-paul-thomas-andersons-one-battle-after-another-what-an-insane-movie/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005061441/https://thefilmstage.com/steven-spielberg-praises-paul-thomas-andersons-one-battle-after-another-what-an-insane-movie/ |archive-date=October 5, 2025 |access-date=September 9, 2025 |website=The Film Stage}}</ref> Instead, Anderson set aside working on an adaptation and envisioned two ideas: one about an "action car-chase movie" and one about a "female revolutionary". ''One Battle After Another'' ultimately emerged as a combination of those two stories with some elements of ''Vineland'', particularly the father-daughter dynamic.<ref name="Vineland"/><ref name="Vineland2">{{cite magazine |last=McGowan |first=Andrew |date=September 26, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' and 'Vineland'— What Paul Thomas Anderson Used and Cut Out of Thomas Pynchon's Novel |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/one-battle-after-another-changes-vineland-1236527544/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930220443/https://variety.com/2025/film/news/one-battle-after-another-changes-vineland-1236527544/ |archive-date=September 30, 2025 |access-date=October 17, 2025 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref name="Vineland3">{{cite web |last=Raup |first=Jordan |date=September 13, 2025 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson on Getting Thomas Pynchon's Blessing to Radically Adapt 'Vineland': 'I Stole the Parts That Really Resonated with Me' |url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-anderson-on-getting-thomas-pynchons-blessing-to-radically-adapt-vineland-i-stole-the-parts-that-really-resonated-with-me/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002184001/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-anderson-on-getting-thomas-pynchons-blessing-to-radically-adapt-vineland-i-stole-the-parts-that-really-resonated-with-me/ |archive-date=October 2, 2025 |access-date=December 22, 2025 |website=The Film Stage}}</ref>

To land the role of Willa Ferguson, the teenage daughter of the film's central character, Infiniti went through a six-month audition process involving multiple callbacks and camera tests as well as chemistry reads with DiCaprio and Hall. The reads were designed to gauge the rapport between the then-newcomer and her potential castmates, but, said Infiniti, "They felt like the coolest kind of masterclass. I remember leaving the room thinking, 'I would love this part, but even if I don't get it, I'll take that with me forever.{{'"}} Infiniti had also been a kickboxing trainer, but she still spent months training in both karate and mixed martial arts that tested her readiness to do her own stunts and handle some intense scenes with Penn.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/call-chase-infiniti-vanities |title=Need Someone to Play a Famous Actor's Kid? Call Chase Infiniti |last=Ford |first=Rebecca |magazine=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=February 11, 2026 |archive-date=October 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251003054954/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/call-chase-infiniti-vanities |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/chase-infiniti-interview-one-battle-after-another-1236366095/ |title=P.T. Anderson Is Betting It All on Chase Infiniti. No Pressure |last=Rankin |first=Seija |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=September 26, 2025 |access-date=February 11, 2026 |archive-date=January 4, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260104043524/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/chase-infiniti-interview-one-battle-after-another-1236366095/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.screendaily.com/features/the-coolest-kind-of-masterclass-chase-infiniti-on-the-six-month-audition-process-for-one-battle-after-another/5213480.article |title='The coolest kind of masterclass': Chase Infiniti on the six-month audition process for 'One Battle After Another' |last=Hazelton |first=John |magazine=[[Screen International#Screen Daily|Screen Daily]] |date=February 11, 2026 |access-date=February 11, 2026}}</ref> "With Willia {{sic}}, it was anybody who's right", casting director [[Cassandra Kulukundis]] said of the broad criteria Anderson gave her, adding, "Doesn't matter if they've ever acted before, if they're a star, if I found them in school, if I find them on the street. That was a huge net{{snd}}if you were between 12 and 25, I was looking at you." Kulukundis was able to narrow the search when she realized how important the physical demands of the part were to the performance. "The moment I saw [Infiniti] dancing, I don't know how to describe it. She's the most unique looking human being I've ever seen." For Kulukundis, Infiniti's ability to hold her own against DiCaprio was also vital. "We tried [DiCaprio] with a bunch of girls and he was really thoughtful and helpful, and we could see the chemistry with Chase. She just kept passing all the tests."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/craft-considerations/one-battle-after-another-making-of-casting-1235180623/ |title=Cassandra Kulukundis on How a Lifetime of Casting for Paul Thomas Anderson Led to 'One Battle After Another' |last=Hemphill |first=Jim |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=February 20, 2026 |access-date=February 20, 2026 |archive-date=February 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260221002145/https://www.indiewire.com/craft-considerations/one-battle-after-another-making-of-casting-1235180623/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

students were cast as [[Extra (acting)|extras]] for a key scene.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bartlett |first=Amanda |title=Locals spill the secrets of filming 'One Battle After Another' in NorCal |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sf-culture/article/leonardo-dicaprio-movie-northern-california-21051254.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250926211813/https://www.sfgate.com/sf-culture/article/leonardo-dicaprio-movie-northern-california-21051254.php |archive-date=September 26, 2025 |access-date=October 10, 2025 |publisher=[[SFGate]] |url-status=live}}</ref>

On February 3, production moved to [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]], with filming at the Sacramento County Administration Building and [[Sacramento County Superior Court|Sacramento County Courthouse]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Lange |first=Ariane |date=February 4, 2024 |title=Movie crew, director Paul Thomas Anderson film in Sacramento{{snd}}but no sign of DiCaprio |url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/local/article285042972.html |access-date=February 4, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Sacramento Bee]] |archive-date=July 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724003647/https://www.sacbee.com/news/local/article285042972.html |url-status=live}}</ref> A [[Tent city|homeless encampment]] was cleared to allow for filming, sparking controversy.<ref>{{cite web |last=Trubey |first=Devin |date=February 10, 2024 |title=Tents cleared from park ahead of movie filming, Sacramento Homeless Union says |url=https://www.abc10.com/article/news/local/sacramento/sacramento-movie-super-bowl-festivities/103-3c15a421-4cc8-4385-b303-aacb7212898c |access-date=February 11, 2024 |publisher=[[KXTV|ABC 10]] |archive-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240226053019/https://www.abc10.com/article/news/local/sacramento/sacramento-movie-super-bowl-festivities/103-3c15a421-4cc8-4385-b303-aacb7212898c |url-status=live}}</ref> The former Sacramento mansion of Governor [[Ronald Reagan]] was used for exterior shots for the Christmas Adventurers Club's headquarters, tying the film back into the original novel, with Pynchon's focus on Reagan.<ref name="Tapestry"/>

[[File:Mission La Purísima Concepción, 1.jpg|thumb|280x280px|The [[Genetic testing|DNA test]] scene was shot in the church at [[La Purísima Mission]] in [[Lompoc, California]]<ref name="RealCalifornia"/>]]

The production took a two-and-a-half-month break from filming because del Toro had a scheduling conflict with [[Wes Anderson]]'s ''[[The Phoenician Scheme]]'' (shot between March and June 2024). When del Toro arrived fresh off the set of ''The Phoenician Scheme'', with ten days between projects, he stepped into a fast-moving production.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/leonardo-dicaprio-paul-thomas-anderson-production-battle-1236432038/ |title=Leonardo DiCaprio, Paul Thomas Anderson Explain Why They Had to Pause Production on 'One Battle After Another' |last=Ford |first=Lily |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=November 20, 2025 |access-date=December 4, 2025 |archive-date=November 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251128164803/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/leonardo-dicaprio-paul-thomas-anderson-production-battle-1236432038/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Benicio">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/benicio-del-toro-interview-one-battle-after-another-oscars-1236510776/ |title=Benicio del Toro on Bonding with Leo, Rewriting PTA, and His First Oscar Nom in Decades |last=Abramovitch |first=Seth |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=February 23, 2026 |access-date=February 23, 2026 |archive-date=February 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260223173906/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/benicio-del-toro-interview-one-battle-after-another-oscars-1236510776/ |url-status=live}}</ref> "I had 10 days to unpack and pack", del Toro said of the 2024 shoot, adding, "Unpack my character in Wes' movie and then get dressed like Sensei and just go. You don't have time to adjust. If you want to jump on a carousel, you generally want time to run and catch up and then jump in. There was none of that."<ref name="Benicio"/>

On location filming also took place in [[Anza-Borrego Desert State Park]] and [[Borrego Springs, California|Borrego Springs]] in May 2024, and [[El Paso, Texas]], including [[El Paso Streetcar]]s, in June 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sf-culture/article/leo-dicaprio-sean-penn-movie-california-desert-19513034.php |title=Leonardo DiCaprio, Sean Penn shoot explosive car chase in California desert |last=Bartlett |first=Amanda |publisher=[[SFGate]] |date=June 13, 2024 |access-date=June 13, 2024 |archive-date=June 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240630021359/https://www.sfgate.com//sf-culture/article/leo-dicaprio-sean-penn-movie-california-desert-19513034.php |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/entertainment/movies/2024/06/21/warner-bros-film-crew-purchases-from-el-paso-nonprofit/74129662007/ |title=Mysterious Warner Bros. film crew in El Paso: What are they shooting? |last=Paloma |first=Natassia |newspaper=[[El Paso Times]] |date=June 21, 2024 |access-date=June 23, 2024 |archive-date=June 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240622061206/https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/entertainment/movies/2024/06/21/warner-bros-film-crew-purchases-from-el-paso-nonprofit/74129662007/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/awards/one-battle-after-another-el-paso-filming-how-it-was-made/ |title=How Filming in El Paso Gave 'One Battle After Another' a Timely Authenticity {{!}} How I Did It Presented by Warner Bros. ===Cinematography===
The film was shot by [[Michael Bauman (cinematographer)|Michael Bauman]] on [[35 mm movie film]] using [[VistaVision]] cameras, marking his third collaboration with Anderson, following ''[[Phantom Thread]]'' (2017) and ''[[Licorice Pizza]]'' (2021).{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name="Cinematography">{{cite magazine |last=Gilman |first=Greg |date=March 1, 2026 |title=Michael Bauman on His Knife's-Edge Cinematography for 'One Battle After Another' |url=https://www.moviemaker.com/michael-bauman-one-battle-after-another/ |magazine=[[MovieMaker]] |access-date=March 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="DP">{{cite magazine |last=Davids |first=Brian |date=January 22, 2026 |title='One Battle After Another' DP Talks the Highway Chase and If Paul Thomas Anderson Will Ever Use IMAX Cameras |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/one-battle-after-another-highway-chase-paul-thomas-anderson-1236480728/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260122020913/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/one-battle-after-another-highway-chase-paul-thomas-anderson-1236480728/ |archive-date=January 22, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Desowitz |first=Bill |date=March 12, 2025 |title=20 Movies Shot on Film in 2025: Separate Safdie Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and More |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/craft/2025-movies-shot-on-film-kodak-1235100813/ |access-date=March 13, 2025 |website=[[IndieWire]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312171917/https://www.indiewire.com/features/craft/2025-movies-shot-on-film-kodak-1235100813 |archive-date=March 12, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Raup |first=Jordan |date=March 13, 2024 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Next Film Sets August 2025 Release, Including IMAX Theaters |url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-sets-august-2025-release-including-imax-theaters/ |access-date=October 15, 2024 |website=The Film Stage |archive-date=February 2, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250202205012/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-sets-august-2025-release-including-imax-theaters/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Willis |first=David Alexander |date=June 6, 2022 |title=Michael Bauman & Paul Thomas Anderson / 'Licorice Pizza' |url=https://britishcinematographer.co.uk/michael-bauman-paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza/ |access-date=December 22, 2025 |publisher=British Cinematographer |archive-date=September 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250918135121/https://britishcinematographer.co.uk/michael-bauman-paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Boone |first=Christopher |date=November 6, 2017 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson is Not the DP of 'Phantom Thread'. No One Is. |url=https://nofilmschool.com/2017/11/paul-thomas-anderson-not-dp-phantom-thread |access-date=December 22, 2025 |website=No Film School |archive-date=January 4, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260104231914/https://nofilmschool.com/2017/11/paul-thomas-anderson-not-dp-phantom-thread |url-status=live}}</ref>}} Between 75 and 80% of the film was shot on VistaVision.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Wakeman |first=Gregory |date=September 30, 2025 |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/why-are-some-of-the-worlds-best-directors-reviving-this-special-film-format-created-in-the-1950s-180987424/ |title=Why Are Some of the World's Best Directors Reviving This Special Film Format Created in the 1950s? |access-date=September 30, 2025 |magazine=[[Smithsonian (magazine)|Smithsonian]] |archive-date=September 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930220429/https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/why-are-some-of-the-worlds-best-directors-reviving-this-special-film-format-created-in-the-1950s-180987424/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''One Battle After Another'' is notable for utilizing VistaVision cameras; [[Brady Corbet]]'s ''[[The Brutalist]]'' (2024) seemed to revive the high-resolution widescreen 35&nbsp;mm format from the 1950s.<ref name="DP"/><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Har-Even |first=Benny |date=February 28, 2025 |title=From 'Star Wars' to 'The Brutalist': The Return of VistaVision |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/bennyhareven/2025/02/28/from-star-wars-to-the-brutalist-the-return-of-vistavision/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |magazine=[[Forbes]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101084457/https://www.forbes.com/sites/bennyhareven/2025/02/28/from-star-wars-to-the-brutalist-the-return-of-vistavision/ |archive-date=January 1, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Atad |first=Corey |date=November 5, 2025 |title=How VistaVision Became 2025's Hottest Film Format |url=https://www.gq.com/story/how-vistavision-became-2025s-hottest-film-format |access-date=February 8, 2026 |magazine=[[GQ]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251128140841/https://www.gq.com/story/how-vistavision-became-2025s-hottest-film-format |archive-date=November 28, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> "The question was more, 'Is this going to be a reliable enough format for us?' When you see the shots from ''The Brutalist'', [DP] [[Lol Crawley]] has got the camera on a [[tripod]]. It's just sitting there and we weren't going to do anything like that", Bauman said, adding, "''One Battle'' was always going to be about movement. It had to be handheld; it had to be on [[Steadicam]]; it had to be strapped to cars; it had to bounce around."<ref name="DP"/> Bauman described his experience shooting the film as "being on the knife's edge", mostly because it was shot on location instead of a [[sound stage]].<ref name="Cinematography"/>

Bauman revealed that Anderson wanted something in the "vein of '[[1970s in film|70s cinema]]", pointing to films like ''[[The French Connection (film)|The French Connection]]'' (1971) and ''[[The Last Detail]]'' (1973), explaining that this "stylistic roughness" was "essential" for Anderson in telling the story.<ref name="Bauman">{{cite magazine |last=Tangcay |first=Jazz |date=January 20, 2026 |title=How 'One Battle After Another' Cinematographer Michael Bauman Shot the Car Chase Scene Like a Gritty 1970s Film |url=https://variety.com/2026/artisans/news/one-battle-after-another-cinematographer-car-chase-scene-explained-1236636258/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-date=January 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260121163815/https://variety.com/2026/artisans/news/one-battle-after-another-cinematographer-car-chase-scene-explained-1236636258/ |url-status=live}}</ref> According to Bauman, VistaVision "was a response to television that some of the studios were developing. And instead of it being four-[[film perforations|perf]] vertical, like a normal 35&nbsp;millimeter camera, this takes the film and puts it eight-perf horizontal, which allows for a much bigger negative space. Each frame is twice the size. And so it's a much richer image." The format was ideal for capturing some of the action sequences in the film, particularly the final car chase sequence.<ref name="Bauman"/> Bauman further admitted that it was a challenge to figure out how to "blend the richness of VistaVision" to make ''One Battle After Another'' "look like a '70s type of film that felt like a lot of the scenes out of ''The French Connection''". He pushed VistaVision to its limits, while using and testing it, saying, "This camera system hadn't really been used at this quantity of film because we shot about {{convert|1.5|e6ft|km|disp=sqbr|abbr=off}} of film for the project [and] hadn't had that kind of level of film run through it in a long time [...] It really underscores the power of shooting on film and what VistaVision is as far as projecting it. It's really a super resting image that has a strong emotional feel to it. The ability to experience that by going to the theater is really unique."<ref name="Bauman"/>

Regarding the impact and location of the climactic car chase, Bauman said, "The sequence is really a testament to the location being the driving force. When Michael Glazier, the [[location manager]], originally found it, he found it almost like by accident when he was driving after he found the location for the 1776 camp."<ref name="CBR">{{cite web |last=Matassa |first=Caralynn |date=January 22, 2026 |title=The Happy 'Accident' That Led to 'One Battle After Another's' Most Unforgettable Scene (Exclusive) |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-battle-after-another-road-scene-michael-bauman-interview/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources|CBR]] |access-date=January 30, 2026 |archive-date=January 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260124064644/https://www.cbr.com/one-battle-after-another-road-scene-michael-bauman-interview/ |url-status=live}}</ref> To figure out how to capture the scene's "dynamic energy", Bauman and his team worked with Allan Padelford, a veteran [[stunt coordinator]] and [[second unit]] director best known for designing high-octane car-chase action sequences, and his Padelford Camera Car.<ref name="CBR"/>

For the film's color and lighting, Bauman said both he and Anderson referred to the work of Hong Kong filmmaker [[Wong Kar-wai]] and ''[[The Silence of the Lambs (film)|The Silence of the Lambs]]'' (1991) as inspiration. Bauman also revealed that he and Anderson carried a print of ''The French Connection'' with them since they "were always screening film dailies", adding, "Sometimes it was just like, hey, it's time to have a little review, just to make sure your visual palette was in the same direction."<ref>{{cite web |last=Matassa |first=Caralynn |date=January 27, 2026 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson Kept a Film Print of This 55-Year-Old Masterpiece to Reference Daily While Shooting 'One Battle After Another' (Exclusive) |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-battle-after-another-french-connection-style-inspiration-exclusive/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources|CBR]] |access-date=January 30, 2026 |archive-date=January 29, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129171840/https://www.cbr.com/one-battle-after-another-french-connection-style-inspiration-exclusive/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Actor and cinematographer collector [[Giovanni Ribisi]] is thanked in the film's end credits for allowing production to use VistaVision cameras that he had personally restored.<ref name="Vineland"/><ref>{{cite web |last=Seigh |first=Steve |date=October 6, 2025 |title=Why did Giovanni Ribisi get a 'Thank You' credit at the end of PTA's 'One Battle After Another'? |url=https://www.joblo.com/one-bettle-after-another-giovanni-ribisi/ |website=[[JoBlo.com]] |access-date=November 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251006222259/https://www.joblo.com/one-bettle-after-another-giovanni-ribisi/ |archive-date=October 6, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=del Barco |first=Mandalit |author-link=Mandalit del Barco |date=December 11, 2025 |title=Why a classic wide-screen movie format from the 1950s is making a comeback |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/12/10/nx-s1-5601901/why-a-classic-wide-screen-movie-format-from-the-1950s-is-making-a-comeback |publisher=[[NPR]] |access-date=December 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211213000/https://www.npr.org/2025/12/10/nx-s1-5601901/why-a-classic-wide-screen-movie-format-from-the-1950s-is-making-a-comeback |archive-date=December 11, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Post-production===
Editing was completed by [[Andy Jurgensen]], who had previously edited ''Licorice Pizza''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Raup |first=Jordan |date=October 6, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Editor Andy Jurgensen on Cutting Paul Thomas Anderson's Action-Comedy Epic |url=https://thefilmstage.com/one-battle-after-another-editor-andy-jurgensen-on-cutting-paul-thomas-andersons-action-comedy-epic/ |access-date=December 31, 2025 |website=The Film Stage |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206054225/https://thefilmstage.com/one-battle-after-another-editor-andy-jurgensen-on-cutting-paul-thomas-andersons-action-comedy-epic/ |archive-date=December 6, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> As a frequent collaborator of Anderson's, Jurgensen knew how to best be "fluid" in his work on the film to match his director's sensibilities. Discussing the final car chase sequence, Jurgensen said, "It was shot over a number of days and there really weren't [[storyboard]]s for it, [Anderson] just had ideas for the beginning, middle, and end. It was really a matter of shooting the cars from the different perspectives [...] We just had to make sure we had all the pieces. I did a string out of all the different perspectives as we were shooting the scenes so that we made sure that we had good moments from all the angles, then it was finding the best bits and starting to assemble. It was just a long sequence going through all of Willa's shots of her eyes, looking at both the rear-view mirror and the side view mirror looking behind at the reflections. You're just slowly kind of whittling down the best fits."<ref>{{cite web |last=Fleming |first=Ryan |date=October 28, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Editor Andy Jurgensen on Balancing Genres & Being 'Fluid' in the Edit |url=https://deadline.com/2025/10/one-battle-after-another-andy-jurgensen-editing-interview-1236600480/ |access-date=December 31, 2025 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113093729/https://deadline.com/2025/10/one-battle-after-another-andy-jurgensen-editing-interview-1236600480/ |archive-date=November 13, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Jurgensen further explained that "it evolved to be what the final [edit] was" and that he was "still adding elements in the final mix", adding, "We went through many edits, but in the [[test screening]]s, it was always people's favorite part."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Dowling |first=Amber |date=March 3, 2026 |title='Nothing is Off the Table': Editor Andy Jurgensen on the Controlled Chaos of 'One Battle After Another' |url=https://www.moviemaker.com/andy-jurgensen-one-battle-after-another/ |magazine=[[MovieMaker]] |access-date=March 3, 2026}}</ref>

Additionally, Jurgensen was on location and got to view dailies with Anderson on a vintage VistaVision horizontal projector, which they borrowed from Warner Bros. "I was the only one traveling from editorial, and then I could supervise setting up the screening room and be there for all the screenings, which was really helpful", said Jurgensen. "And then while they were shooting, I also brought my computer system, getting digital dailies and making more notes, assembling stuff. You're with the crew and it's just so much better. You understand what everyone's going through and you're part of the process. But that's Paul's style."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Desowitz |first=Bill |date=December 4, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Editor Talks Getting 'Woozy' Cutting Together that Climactic Car Chase |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/one-battle-after-another-editor-car-chase-1236435299/ |access-date=December 31, 2025 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251204220426/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/one-battle-after-another-editor-car-chase-1236435299/ |archive-date=December 4, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2024, ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' reported that the film had been [[Greenlight|greenlit]] with a $115&nbsp;million [[production budget]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Siegel |first=Tatiana |date=February 21, 2024 |title=Warner Bros. Spends Big: 'Joker 2' Budget Hits $200 Million, Lady Gaga's $12 Million Payday, Courting Tom Cruise's New Deal, and More |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/warner-bros-spending-joker-2-budget-tom-cruise-deal-1235917640/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221181608/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/warner-bros-spending-joker-2-budget-tom-cruise-deal-1235917640/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=February 21, 2024 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> In August 2024, ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reported the budget was "more than $140&nbsp;million", noting that Anderson's highest-grossing film, ''[[There Will Be Blood]]'' (2007), only made $76&nbsp;million, but that "Warner executives say DiCaprio's box-office track record justifies the budget for Anderson".<ref>{{cite news |last=Flint |first=Joe |date=August 10, 2024 |title=At Warner Discovery It's Lean Times, Except for the Movie Studio Bosses |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/at-warner-discovery-its-lean-times-except-for-the-movie-studio-bosses-8fc1d3f6 |access-date=August 11, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url-access=subscription}}</ref> That month, sources indicated the film had been titled ''The Battle of Baktan Cross'' as rumors circulated that it was loosely inspired by Pynchon's ''Vineland''; Anderson previously adapted Pynchon's ''[[Inherent Vice]]'' (2009) into a [[Inherent Vice (film)|feature film in 2014]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.gq.com/story/is-paul-thomas-andersons-mysterious-big-budget-new-leonardo-dicaprio-film-an-imax-thomas-pynchon-movie |title=Is Paul Thomas Anderson's Mysterious, Big-Budget New Leonardo DiCaprio Film an IMAX Thomas Pynchon Movie? |last=Rindner |first=Grant |magazine=[[GQ]] |date=March 22, 2024 |access-date=August 5, 2024 |url-access=limited |archive-date=August 5, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240805202025/https://www.gq.com/story/is-paul-thomas-andersons-mysterious-big-budget-new-leonardo-dicaprio-film-an-imax-thomas-pynchon-movie |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://featurefirst.net/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-will-be-titled-the-battle-of-baktan-cross/ |title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Next Film Will Be Titled 'The Battle of Baktan Cross' |last=Gubecka |first=Zanda |website=Feature First |date=August 2, 2024 |access-date=December 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812103310/https://featurefirst.net/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-will-be-titled-the-battle-of-baktan-cross/ |archive-date=August 12, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://filmstories.co.uk/news/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-reportedly-called-the-battle-of-baktan-cross/ |title=Paul Thomas Anderson's next film reportedly called 'The Battle of Baktan Cross' |last=Lambie |first=Ryan |website=Film Stories |date=August 2, 2024 |access-date=December 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811084845/https://filmstories.co.uk/news/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-reportedly-called-the-battle-of-baktan-cross/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

By August 2025, ''Variety'' reported the film's final budget as $175&nbsp;million, while Warner Bros. said it cost $130&nbsp;million.<ref name="Budget"/> The film is the most costly of Anderson's career.<ref>{{cite web |last=Welk |first=Brian |date=September 25, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' is Unique in Paul Thomas Anderson's Filmography{{snd}}and So Are Its Box Office Chances |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/box-office/paul-thomas-anderson-one-battle-after-another-box-office-1235152232/ |access-date=December 15, 2025 |website=[[IndieWire]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925133231/https://www.indiewire.com/news/box-office/paul-thomas-anderson-one-battle-after-another-box-office-1235152232/ |archive-date=September 25, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' reported that [[Below-the-line (filmmaking)|below-the-line]], on location shooting in California cost $101.6&nbsp;million, with a [[tax credit]] of $8.4&nbsp;million.<ref name="Opening">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2025/09/box-office-one-battle-after-another-1236556684/ |title='One Battle After Another' at $22M+ Reps Record Debut for Paul Thomas Anderson; Leonardo DiCaprio's 11th Movie to Open to $20M+{{snd}}Box Office |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=September 28, 2025 |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |access-date=September 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250926062327/https://deadline.com/2025/09/box-office-one-battle-after-another-1236556684/ |archive-date=September 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> By September 2025, ''Variety'' reported that an additional $70&nbsp;million was spent on [[marketing]].<ref name="BoxOffice">{{cite magazine |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=September 28, 2025 |title=Box Office: Leonardo DiCaprio's 'One Battle After Another' Kicks Off with $22 Million |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/box-office/box-office-one-battle-after-another-opening-weekend-leonardo-dicaprio-1236533304/ |access-date=December 22, 2025 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250928161057/https://variety.com/2025/film/box-office/box-office-one-battle-after-another-opening-weekend-leonardo-dicaprio-1236533304/ |archive-date=September 28, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Beginning in January 2025, the film had multiple test screenings, which reinforced the rumored connection to ''Vineland''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Raup |first=Jordan |date=January 25, 2025 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another' Test Screens, Confirmed to Be Modern Update on 'Vineland' |url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-one-battle-after-another-test-screens-confirmed-to-be-modern-update-on-vineland/ |website=The Film Stage |access-date=January 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125004230/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-one-battle-after-another-test-screens-confirmed-to-be-modern-update-on-vineland/ |archive-date=January 25, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> It marked the first time since ''[[Boogie Nights]]'' (1997) that Anderson agreed to audience testing; based on the feedback, he cut eight to ten minutes.<ref name="DeLucaAbdy">{{cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/mike-deluca-pam-abdy-warner-bros-movie-flops-1236351128/ |title=Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy Under Fire at Warner Bros. Amid Box Office Flops: 'We Didn't Want to Fail' David Zaslav (Exclusive) |last=Donnelly |first=Matt |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=March 28, 2025 |access-date=March 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250328195023/https://variety.com/2025/film/news/mike-deluca-pam-abdy-warner-bros-movie-flops-1236351128/ |archive-date=March 28, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> There was also a report that Warner Bros. was working with Anderson to refine the film, but did not ask for radical changes.<ref name="Jurgensen">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/movies/one-battle-after-another-editor-andy-jurgensen-interview/ |title='One Battle After Another' Editor Andy Jurgensen Shares Secrets from Paul Thomas Anderson's Masterpiece |last=Taylor |first=Drew |magazine=[[TheWrap]] |date=February 4, 2026 |access-date=February 5, 2026 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=February 4, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260204181505/https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/movies/one-battle-after-another-editor-andy-jurgensen-interview/ |url-status=live}}</ref> "We trimmed it down and that was just our normal process", Jurgensen said. According to Jurgensen, Anderson does not like to test his films, but it was something that Warner Bros. requested. Anderson partially agreed to the test screenings because he wanted to know if it played well as a comedy, and, as Jurgensen said, "There are some sensitive things in the movie, both racial things and political things. It was going to be interesting for us to test it in different parts of the country." Jurgensen also added that the tests confirmed that "the humor was working. And luckily, it did confirm, when you're kind of trying to figure out, 'How can we push it a little further? How can we do things?{{'"}}<ref name="Jurgensen"/> He further noted that the studio was not trying to enforce an ultimatum and did not pressure them to cut anything, saying, "They were supportive. I think the test screenings helped us because they were reacting so well to it."<ref name="Jurgensen"/>

The film's title was officially confirmed in March 2025, with Warner Bros. debuting a [[teaser trailer]].<ref name="Teaser">{{cite web |last=Goodfellow |first=Melanie |date=March 27, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Trailer: Leonardo DiCaprio Searches for His Daughter in Paul Thomas Anderson's Gunslinger Thriller for Warner Bros |url=https://deadline.com/video/one-battle-after-another-teaser-leonardo-dicaprio/ |access-date=April 1, 2025 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250322195603/https://deadline.com/video/one-battle-after-another-teaser-leonardo-dicaprio/ |archive-date=March 22, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''One Battle After Another'' marked Anderson's sixth feature film collaboration with composer and [[Radiohead]] guitarist [[Jonny Greenwood]],<ref>{{cite news |last=Lewis |first=John |date=May 10, 2024 |title=Jonny Greenwood: 'I'm still arsing around on instruments like when I was a kid' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/article/2024/may/10/jonny-greenwood-im-still-arsing-around-on-instruments-like-when-i-was-a-kid |access-date=May 11, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |issn=0261-3077 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510041641/https://www.theguardian.com/music/article/2024/may/10/jonny-greenwood-im-still-arsing-around-on-instruments-like-when-i-was-a-kid |archive-date=May 10, 2024 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live}}</ref> and the sixth with Anderson and first [[assistant director]] and producer [[Adam Somner]], who died in November 2024; the film is dedicated to Somner.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/adam-somner-dead-first-ad-steven-spielberg-ridley-scott-1236189709/ |title=Adam In February 2026, ''Variety'' reported that the awards campaign budget for the film was approximately $14&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/awards/sinners-one-battle-after-another-oscar-campaigns-warner-bros-1236660361/ |title=Warner Bros' $30 Million Oscars Race: How 'Sinners' and 'One Battle After Another' Are Campaigning at the Same Studio |last=Davis |first=Clayton |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=February 13, 2026 |archive-date=February 13, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260213025251/https://variety.com/2026/film/awards/sinners-one-battle-after-another-oscar-campaigns-warner-bros-1236660361/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Marketing==
The marketing campaign for ''One Battle After Another'' cost $70&nbsp;million.<ref name="BoxOffice"/> On March 27, 2025, DiCaprio launched his own [[YouTube]] channel with the debut of the [[teaser trailer]].<ref name="Teaser"/> Extended footage of the film was shown during the Warner Bros. presentation at [[CinemaCon]] in April 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2025/04/leonardo-dicaprio-one-battle-after-another-warner-bros-1236356485/ |title=Leonardo DiCaprio Kicks Off Warner Bros' CinemaCon with More Footage from Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another' |last1=D'Alessandro |first1=Anthony |last2=Tartaglione |first2=Nancy |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=April 1, 2025 |access-date=February 25, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250402005615/https://deadline.com/2025/04/leonardo-dicaprio-one-battle-after-another-warner-bros-1236356485/ |archive-date=April 2, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> The second trailer for the film was released online on July 24, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/trailers/one-battle-after-another-new-trailer-1235140806/ |title='One Battle After Another' New Trailer: Leonardo DiCaprio is a Vigilante with No Fear in PTA's 10th Movie |last=Lattanzio |first=Ryan |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=July 24, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724140101/https://www.indiewire.com/news/trailers/one-battle-after-another-new-trailer-1235140806/ |archive-date=July 24, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> That same day, a video announcement, via the ''One Battle After Another'' [[Instagram]] account, announced the film was coming to ''[[Fortnite Creative]]'' on September 12.<ref>{{cite Instagram |postid=DMfijEuuQt6 |user=onebattleafteranothermovie |title=There are no hands on the clock. #OneBattleAfterAnother x Fortnite coming soon. |date=July 24, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Fortnite">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/you-will-never-guess-what-fortnites-latest-movie-collab-is-with/1100-6533417/ |title=You Will Never Guess What Fortnite's Latest Movie Collab is With |last=Compendio |first=Chris |website=[[GameSpot]] |date=July 24, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |archive-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116041431/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/you-will-never-guess-what-fortnites-latest-movie-collab-is-with/1100-6533417/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite Instagram |postid=DOOjJ0YDoa5 |user=onebattleafteranothermovie |title='One Battle After Another' is coming to Fortnite Creative before you can bat an eyelash! Creator island launching September 12th. |date=September 5, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026}}</ref> Additionally, posts on [[X (social network)|Twitter]] that applied meme templates to out-of-context clips from the film were released.<ref name="Marketing">{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1978604/why-one-battle-after-another-marketing-campaign-brilliant/ |title=Why 'One Battle After Another's' Confusing Marketing Has Secretly Been Brilliant |last=Bilodeau |first=Quinn |website=[[/Film|SlashFilm]] |date=September 26, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |archive-date=February 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260220140001/https://www.slashfilm.com/1978604/why-one-battle-after-another-marketing-campaign-brilliant/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Multiple film critics and news outlets found the marketing to be "confusing" and "unusual".{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name="Fortnite"/><ref name="Marketing"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/leonardo-dicaprio-fortnite.html |title=Sorry, Is Leonardo DiCaprio About to Be in Fortnite? |last=Hoepfner |first=Fran |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]] |date=July 25, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pajiba.com/news/the-fortnite-marketing-for-paul-thomas-andersons-new-movie-is-so-weird.php |title=Why is the Marketing for Paul Thomas Anderson's New Movie So Weird? |last=Sanford |first=Andrew |website=Pajiba |date=September 11, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1982077/one-battle-after-another-fortnite-crossover-lockjaw-dynamite-dolpin/ |title='One Battle After Another's' Bizarre Fortnite Crossover is Even Stranger After You've Seen the Movie |last=Bilodeau |first=Quinn |website=[[/Film|SlashFilm]] |date=September 30, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |archive-date=October 9, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251009012052/https://www.slashfilm.com/1982077/one-battle-after-another-fortnite-crossover-lockjaw-dynamite-dolpin/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://theankler.com/p/paul-thomas-anderson-fortnite-crowd-pleaser-letterboxd-issue-2 |title=How Paul Thomas Anderson Landed in Fortnite, as the Movies-as-Games Era Arrives |last=Frank |first=Matthew |website=[[The Ankler]] |date=November 26, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026}}</ref>}} Dana Nussbaum, Warner Bros. Pictures co-head of global motion picture marketing, defended this approach to promoting the film, stating, "Every campaign must be bespoke and you have to quickly shift based on what the audience is telling you", adding, "The audience moves really fast and you have to be moving at the same pace."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/leonardo-dicaprio-one-battle-after-another-tiktok-campaign-1236392770/ |title=How Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another' Brought Leonardo DiCaprio to TikTok |last=Gardner |first=Chris |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=October 3, 2025 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |archive-date=February 25, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260225134300/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/leonardo-dicaprio-one-battle-after-another-tiktok-campaign-1236392770/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release==
===Theatrical===
[[File:Vista Theater Presenting One Battle After Another in VistaVision Sign.jpg|thumb|[[VistaVision]] presentation at [[Vista Theatre (Los Angeles)|Vista Theatre]]]]

The film was released on September 26, 2025, following previews on September 24.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/maggie-gyllenhaal-the-bride-moves-out-of-2025-1236168657/ |title=Maggie Gyllenhaal's 'The Bride' Moves Out of 2025, Paul Thomas Anderson's Next Movie Pushed to Late September |last=McClintock |first=Pamela |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=March 19, 2025 |access-date=March 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250320013330/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/maggie-gyllenhaal-the-bride-moves-out-of-2025-1236168657/ |archive-date=March 20, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> It is the first of Anderson's films to be released in [[IMAX]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-anderson-selects-five-films-to-watch-ahead-of-one-battle-after-another-as-tickets-go-on-sale/ |title=Paul Thomas Anderson Selects Five Films to Watch Ahead of 'One Battle After Another' as Tickets Go on Sale |last=Pearce |first=Leonard |website=The Film Stage |date=September 3, 2025 |access-date=September 9, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250903150156/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-anderson-selects-five-films-to-watch-ahead-of-one-battle-after-another-as-tickets-go-on-sale/ |archive-date=September 3, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> The film was previously set to be released on August 8, 2025, but was moved for a potential [[awards season]] campaign.<ref name="DeLucaAbdy"/><ref name="Release">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/03/the-batman-2-release-date-2026-1235856229/ |title='The Batman 2' from Matt Reeves Heads to Fall 2026; Paul Thomas Anderson-Leonardo DiCaprio Movie Gets Summer 2025 Date |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=March 12, 2024 |access-date=March 12, 2024 |archive-date=March 12, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312181422/https://deadline.com/2024/03/the-batman-2-release-date-2026-1235856229/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="MovieChiefs">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/warner-bros-movie-chiefs-michael-de-luca-and-pamela-abdy-1236365062/ |title='One Battle After Another' Ends for Warner Bros. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250910020559/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/warner-bros-movie-chiefs-michael-de-luca-and-pamela-abdy-1236365062/ |url-status=live |quote=Sources say Warners intends on launching an awards campaign.}}</ref> It premiered at the [[TCL Chinese Theatre]] in Los Angeles on September 8, 2025, and had a global tour beginning in London on September 16, in Mexico City on September 18, and ending in New York City on September 21.<ref>{{cite Instagram |postid=DN3UaXzXMK6 |user=onebattleafteranothermovie |title=All roads lead to #OneBattleAfterAnother only in theaters and IMAX September 26. |date=August 27, 2025 |access-date=September 12, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Tapp |first=Tom |date=September 8, 2025 |title='One |archive-date=November 26, 2025 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

''One Battle After Another'' was projected in the VistaVision format, with screenings at the [[Vista Theatre (Los Angeles)|Vista Theatre]] in Los Angeles, [[Regal Cinemas|Regal]] Union Square 17 in New York, [[Coolidge Corner Theatre]] in Brookline, and [[Odeon Luxe Leicester Square]] in London.<ref name="Formats"/> The film was also released in other formats, including [[4DX]], [[digital IMAX]], [[Dolby Vision]], [[IMAX#Projectors|IMAX 70 mm]], and standard [[70 mm film]].<ref name="Formats">{{cite magazine |last=Tangcay |first=Jazz |date=September 26, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Formats: What is VistaVision and What Are All the Ways to Watch? In January 2026, it was reported that the film would return to select IMAX 70&nbsp;mm locations to celebrate its [[98th Academy Awards|Academy Award nominations]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Shanfeld |first=Ethan |date=January 23, 2026 |title='Sinners' and 'One Battle After Another' Returning to IMAX 70mm After Oscar Nominations (Exclusive) |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/sinners-one-battle-after-another-imax-70mm-1236638034/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=January 23, 2026 |archive-date=January 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260123193621/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/sinners-one-battle-after-another-imax-70mm-1236638034/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

was released on [[Disney+ Hotstar|JioHotstar]] in India on February 26, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last=Behera |first=Pritinanda |date=February 26, 2026 |title=JioHotstar, SonyLiv, ZEE5 This Week: 'One Battle After Another', 'Bugonia', and more |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/entertainment/ott/story/jiohotstar-sonyliv-zee5-this-week-one-battle-after-another-bugonia-and-more-2874252-2026-02-25 |access-date=February 26, 2026 |newspaper=[[India Today]]}}</ref> Streaming analytics firm ''FlixPatrol'', which monitors daily updated [[Video on demand|VOD]] charts and streaming ratings across the globe, reported that ''One Battle After Another'' became the most-streamed film on HBO Max within the first four days of its release in December 2025. The film also ranked as the No. 1 film globally on the streaming service as of December 23.<ref>{{cite web |last=Valentine |first=Evan |date=December 23, 2025 |title=HBO Max Added One of the Best Movies of 2025 and It's Already a Streaming Hit |url=https://comicbook.com/movies/news/hbo-max-added-one-of-the-best-movies-of-2025-and-its-already-a-streaming-hit/ |access-date=December 24, 2025 |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111205141/https://comicbook.com/movies/news/hbo-max-added-one-of-the-best-movies-of-2025-and-its-already-a-streaming-hit/ |archive-date=January 11, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> It became available to stream on HBO Max in the United Kingdom on March 26, 2026; UK-based viewers are also able to stream the film via [[Now (streaming service)|NOW]] and [[Sky Cinema]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Warner |first=Sam |date=March 26, 2026 |title='Masterpiece' thriller 'One Battle After Another' is finally available to stream in the UK |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a70853596/one-battle-after-another-stream-uk/ |access-date=March 26, 2026 |publisher=[[Digital Spy]]}}</ref>

Following the film's success at the [[98th Academy Awards]], where it won six Oscars (including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]]), it received newfound success on the [[Apple TV (streaming service)|Apple TV]] store, despite being available to stream on HBO Max. ''FlixPatrol'' reported that the film's [[Video on demand#Premium|PVOD]] success on [[iTunes]] surged, with it hitting #1 in the United States as of March 17, 2026, where it also topped the charts in 33 other countries.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fang |first=Sam |date=March 18, 2026 |title=Leonardo DiCaprio's $210M R-Rated Action Thriller Becomes a Streaming Sensation on a Surprising Platform After Oscar Win |url=https://www.cbr.com/leonardo-dicaprio-one-battle-after-another-apple-tv-success-mar-2026/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=[[Comic Book Resources|CBR]]}}</ref>

On June 2, 2026, ''One Battle After Another'' was released as a collectible 4K UHD Blu-ray [[SteelBook]].<ref>{{cite web |title=One Battle After Another 4K Blu-ray (SteelBook) |url=https://www.blu-ray.com/movies/One-Battle-After-Another-4K-Blu-ray/397881/ |access-date=March 20, 2026 |website=Blu-ray.com}}</ref> It includes new bonus features and behind-the-scenes materials curated by Anderson, including camera, lighting and costume tests, a screen test from Infiniti, and a feature-length "making-of" documentary. Additional extras include a deep dive into the editing process and footage from the film's opening night at the Vista Theatre, plus a 24-page booklet of behind-the-scenes photography.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Tingley |first=Anna |date=March 19, 2026 |title='One Battle After Another' Sets New Blu-ray Release Featuring Screen Tests, Behind-the-Scenes Footage, and Photography Book |url=https://variety.com/2026/shopping/news/one-battle-after-another-blu-ray-behind-the-scenes-bonus-1236693462/ |access-date=March 20, 2026 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
''One Battle After Another'' grossed $72.9&nbsp;million in the U.S. and Canada, and $140.3&nbsp;million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $213.2&nbsp;million.<ref name=BOM/><ref name=NUM/> The film ended up being a [[Box-office bomb|box office failure]], falling short of its estimated $300&nbsp;million break-even point and losing Warner Bros. an estimated $100 million during its theatrical run.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite web |last=Barber |first=Nicholas |date=October 22, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another': Why this year's most acclaimed film flopped |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20251020-why-one-battle-after-another-flopped |access-date=December 16, 2025 |publisher=[[BBC]] |archive-date=December 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251230081157/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20251020-why-one-battle-after-another-flopped |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="$200 Million">{{cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/now-you-see-me-3-global-box-office-demon-slayer-one-battle-after-another-1236583164/ |title='Now You See Me 3' Tops Global Box Office with $75.5 Million, 'Demon Slayer' Hits $730 Million, 'One Battle After Another' Crosses $200 Million |last=Lang |first=Brent |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=November 16, 2025 |access-date=December 3, 2025 |archive-date=November 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118042024/https://variety.com/2025/film/news/now-you-see-me-3-global-box-office-demon-slayer-one-battle-after-another-1236583164/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Maher |first=Kevin |date=December 8, 2025 |title=Golden Globes nominations 2026: Has 'Wicked' been snubbed? In the U.S. and Canada, the film opened in 3,634 theaters, the widest release for a film directed by Anderson and his first to debut in wide release.<ref name="HighestGrossingFilm"/><ref>{{cite 27, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> It made $8.8&nbsp;million on its first day, including $3.1&nbsp;million from Thursday previews.<ref name="Opening Weekend"/><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Moreau |first=Jordan |date=September 26, 2025 |title=Box Office: Leonardo DiCaprio's 'One Battle After Another' Makes $3.1 Million in Previews |url-status=live}}</ref> The film earned $22&nbsp;million over the weekend, topping the box office, and handily marking the best weekend for a film directed by Anderson, topping the $4.9&nbsp;million earned by ''There Will Be Blood'' in its fifth weekend in 2008.<ref name="Opening"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Weekend projections: 'One Battle After Another' and 'Gabby's Dollhouse' hoping for good |archive-date=September 30, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> In its second weekend, ''One Battle After Another'' grossed $11&nbsp;million (a drop of 50%), finishing second behind then-newcomer ''[[Taylor |access-date=December 22, 2025 |quote=A wave of early reactions hit the internet, including a very strong response from fellow director [[Steven Spielberg]], who doesn't often gush about recent
