{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|94|8.9|448|An epic screwball adventure teeming with awe-inspiring action set pieces, ''One Battle After Another'' is Paul Thomas Anderson's most entertaining film yet while also one of his most thematically rich.|ref=yes|access-date=October 26, 2026}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 95 out of 100, based on 63 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''One Battle After Another'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/one-battle-after-another |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=December 1, 2025 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "A" on its A+ to F scale, while those at [[PostTrak]] rated the film four-and-a-half out of five stars, with 74% of audiences saying they would "definitely recommend" it.<ref name="Opening"/>

[[Owen Gleiberman]] of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' wrote that the film "taps into the fierce urgency of now; it gives you a chill that's also a wake-up call", adding that it "has the kind of twists and turns that feed the audience, giving us the childlike sensation that we have no idea what's coming next, and that that's the happiest way there is to watch a movie". Brian Tallerico of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' wrote that ''One Battle After Another'' "is a timeless story of resistance, one that playfully weaves together influences as broad-reaching as the true story of [[Weather Underground]] and cinematic depictions of rebellion, but it's also a remarkably propulsive, fun, and eventually moving piece of work about the human beings caught up in the chaotic machine".<ref name="RogerEbert.com">{{cite web |last=Tallerico |first=Brian |title='One Battle After Another' movie review (2025) |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/one-battle-after-another-movie-review-2025 |date=September 25, 2025 |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917163917/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/one-battle-after-another-movie-review-2025 |archive-date=September 17, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Justin Chang]] of ''[[The New Yorker]]'' called the film "a father-daughter epic, with an unusually personal gush of feeling. You can count on one hand the number of scenes that Bob and Willa share, but their connection{{snd}}a swirl of protectiveness, exasperation, and fiercely unconditional love{{snd}}binds the movie and its madly whirling parts together".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Chang |first=Justin |author-link=Justin Chang |date=September 26, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' is a Powerhouse of Tenderness and Fury |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2025/10/06/one-battle-after-another-movie-review |access-date=October 4, 2025 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |url-access=subscription |archive-date=September 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250926101935/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2025/10/06/one-battle-after-another-movie-review |url-status=live}}</ref>

Katie Walsh of the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' called the film a "searing indictment of this particular moment in American history" by which "Anderson balances the sprawling, conspiracy-minded aspects of this yarn with the intimate father-daughter story, which is the heart of the matter".<ref>{{cite news |last=Walsh |first=Katie |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2025/09/25/review-one-battle-after-another-movie/ |title=Review: 'One Battle After Another' is a searing indictment of this American moment |newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=September 25, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |url-access=limited}}</ref> Writing for ''[[The New York Times]]'', [[Manohla Dargis]] called the film "a carnivalesque epic about good and evil, violence and power, inalienable rights and the fight against injustice; it's also a love story. The film speaks to the failures of the past and of the present but insists on the promise of the future".<ref>{{cite news |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |date=September 25, 2025 |author-link=Manohla Dargis |title='One Battle After Another' Review: Paul Thomas Anderson's Rallying Cry |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/25/movies/one-battle-after-another-review-paul-thomas-anderson.html |access-date=October 1, 2025 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250928022411/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/25/movies/one-battle-after-another-review-paul-thomas-anderson.html |archive-date=September 28, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Richard Lawson (writer)|Richard Lawson]] of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' wrote that ''One Battle After Another'' is "a furious film, a richly engaging and persuasive polemic" in which "Anderson shows a previously unseen aptitude for action and suspense; ''One Battle After Another'' is, essentially, a thriller, albeit one teeming with enormous ideas about the collapse and possible rescue of the country".<ref name="Review">{{cite magazine |last=Lawson |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Lawson (writer) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprio-1236372737/ |title='One Battle After Another' Review: Leonardo DiCaprio Leads Paul Thomas Anderson's Bracingly Timely Wonder |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=September 17, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917203251/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprio-1236372737/ |archive-date=September 17, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Alex Saveliev of ''[[Film Threat]]'' opened his review by writing that the film "demands to be seen on the largest screen possible to fully absorb the 35&nbsp;mm VistaVision experience with every cell of your body. Everything about it is grand: its characters, its action sequences, its timely sentiments, even the quieter moments".<ref>{{cite web |last=Saveliev |first=Alex |url=https://filmthreat.com/reviews/one-battle-after-another-action-thriller-review/ |title=One Battle After Another |website=[[Film Threat]] |date=September 18, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007225755/https://filmthreat.com/reviews/one-battle-after-another-action-thriller-review/ |archive-date=October 7, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Peter Bradshaw]], awarding the film five stars and writing for ''[[The Guardian]]'', was effusive in his praise. He celebrated the "riff on the now recognisable Anderson-Pynchonian idea of counterculture and counter-revolution", praised the score by Greenwood, and pondered if the "central paternity crisis triangle [is] an image for an ownership dispute around the American melting-pot dream".<ref>{{cite news |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Bradshaw |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/sep/17/one-battle-after-another-review-paul-thomas-andersons-thrillingly-helter-skelter-counter-culture-caper |title='One Battle After Another' review{{snd}}Paul Thomas Anderson's thrillingly helter-skelter counterculture caper |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=September 17, 2025 |access-date=October 9, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917164117/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/sep/17/one-battle-after-another-review-paul-thomas-andersons-thrillingly-helter-skelter-counter-culture-caper |archive-date=September 17, 2025 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live}}</ref>

The performances of the cast were also highly praised.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite web |last=Ried |first=Joe |date=December 1, 2025 |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/best-actor-actress-acting-movie-performances-2025.html |title=The Best Film Performances of 2025 |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]] |access-date=January 22, 2026 |url-access=limited |archive-date=February 2, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202031718/https://www.vulture.com/article/best-actor-actress-acting-movie-performances-2025.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="RollingStoneBestPerformances"/><ref name="VanityFairBestPerformances"/><ref name="THRBestPerformances"/><ref>{{cite web |author=The Film Stage |date=December 11, 2025 |url=https://thefilmstage.com/the-best-performances-of-2025/ |title=The Best Performances of 2025 |website=The Film Stage |access-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-date=January 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260103051101/https://thefilmstage.com/the-best-performances-of-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Welch |first1=Alex |last2=Taylor |first2=Drew |date=December 21, 2025 |url=https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/movies/best-movie-performances-of-2025/ |title=The 11 Best Movie Performances of 2025 |magazine=[[TheWrap]] |access-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-date=December 21, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251221175032/https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/movies/best-movie-performances-of-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Collider Staff |date=December 22, 2025 |url=https://collider.com/best-movie-performances-2025/ |title=The Best Movie Performances of 2025 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-date=January 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260121015740/https://collider.com/best-movie-performances-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Cavanaugh |first=Patrick |date=December 23, 2025 |url=https://movieweb.com/best-movie-performances-2025-sinners-bugonia-one-battle-after-another/ |title=The Best Movie Performances of 2025 |website=[[MovieWeb]] |access-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208173559/https://movieweb.com/best-movie-performances-2025-sinners-bugonia-one-battle-after-another/ |url-status=live}}</ref>}} Gleiberman also added that "Anderson knows that the quality that liberates DiCaprio is comedy. By having him play Bob as a dissolute stoner addict, discombobulated by his loss of faith, he humanizes DiCaprio and coaxes a great performance out of him."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Gleiberman |first=Owen |author-link=Owen Gleiberman |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/reviews/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprio-sean-penn-1236520520/ |title='One Battle After Another' Review: Leonardo DiCaprio and Sean Penn Are Brilliant in Paul Thomas Anderson's Mesmerizing Vision of a Police-State America |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=September 17, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917162231/https://variety.com/2025/film/reviews/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprio-sean-penn-1236520520/ |archive-date=September 17, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Tallerico of ''RogerEbert.com'' felt DiCaprio gives a "carefully modulated" performance, but he nevertheless singled out Sean Penn's performance as "his best work in years", writing he "flexes his muscles, grits his teeth, and growls his lines, but somehow threads the needle between truth and caricature".<ref name="RogerEbert.com"/> David Sims of ''[[The Atlantic]]'' opined, "Penn, giving a brilliant performance of cold villainy that could win him a third [[Academy Awards|Oscar]], is unafraid of lancing the inherent goofiness of a [[Fascism|fascist]]. DiCaprio plays Bob as a sweetheart rather than a buffoon; he's a tired, strung-out [[antihero]] made weary not by his yearslong efforts to fight back but by the relentlessness of the world."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Sims |first=David |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2025/09/one-battle-after-another-movie-review/684262/ |title=A Movie Touching One Raw Nerve After Another |magazine=[[The Atlantic]] |date=September 18, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250918205226/https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2025/09/one-battle-after-another-movie-review/684262/ |archive-date=September 18, 2025 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live}}</ref> [[David Ehrlich]] of ''[[IndieWire]]'' praised "magnetically self-possessed newcomer/instant movie star Chase Infiniti, whose performance inspires a strange kind of secondhand pride". He also singled out the performances of Penn and Taylor, calling the latter "eruptive [...] steaming with revolutionary zeal" and the former "career-best".<ref>{{cite web |last=Ehrlich |first=David |author-link=David Ehrlich |date=September 17, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Review: Paul Thomas Anderson Returns to the Modern World with a Blisteringly Hilarious Dad-Core Masterpiece |url=https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/one-battle-after-another-movie-review-paul-thomas-anderson-1235151707/ |access-date=October 8, 2025 |website=[[IndieWire]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917163951/https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/one-battle-after-another-movie-review-paul-thomas-anderson-1235151707/ |archive-date=September 17, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]''{{'}}s Pete Hammond called Penn's performance "a riot to watch" while considering the performance of Taylor as "dazzling" and "unforgettable".<ref name="Hammond"/>

William Bibbiani of ''[[TheWrap]]'' was less enthusiastic, describing the plot as scattershot, unfocused, overly long, and the film's themes as shallow, writing that Anderson was "more interested in taking cheap potshots at the film's real-world analogues than actually exploring them".<ref name="TheWrap">{{cite magazine |last=Bibbiani |first=William |date=September 17, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another' Review: Leonardo DiCaprio Lebowskis His Way Through the Revolution |url=https://www.thewrap.com/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprio-paul-thomas-anderson/ |magazine=[[TheWrap]] |access-date=October 2, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917225316/https://www.thewrap.com/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprio-paul-thomas-anderson/ |archive-date=September 17, 2025 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |quote=Perfidia is a charismatic figurehead and an insatiable sex addict, which to Anderson makes her dangerously irresponsible. Worse, she's also a sex criminal who forces the right wing Colonel Steven J. Lockjaw to pleasure himself at gunpoint during a raid.}}</ref> ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]''{{'}}s [[Kyle Smith (critic)|Kyle Smith]] similarly noted the film is "big and brash. Rangy in tone, style and theme, it has so much going on that a single viewing hardly seems sufficient to absorb it all. Whether it's a masterpiece or a hodgepodge will be a matter of some discussion; the reach is evident but the grasp is a little shaky".<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Kyle |author-link=Kyle Smith (critic) |url=https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/film/one-battle-after-another-review-leonardo-dicaprios-rusty-revolutionary-87468232 |title='One Battle After Another' Review: Paul Thomas Anderson's Rusty Revolutionary |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=September 25, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Israeli media-critic [[Liel Leibovitz]] of ''[[The Free Press (CBS News)|The Free Press]]'' described the film as "irredeemable" and "just another sign that Hollywood has once again driven itself to total moral, artistic, and creative ruin".<ref>{{cite web |last=Leibovitz |first=Liel |author-link=Liel Leibovitz |date=March 13, 2026 |title='One Battle After Another' is Irredeemable |url=https://www.thefp.com/p/one-battle-after-another-is-irredeemable |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Free Press (CBS News)|The Free Press]] |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Author [[Bret Easton Ellis]] dismissed the praise, arguing that the film, in which he found a "liberal mustiness," is a hit with critics only because it aligns with a "leftist sensibility."<ref>{{cite news |last=Sharf|first=Zack  |date=October 10, 2025 |title=''One Battle After Another'' Is a Hit with Critics Because It 'Aligns with a Leftist Sensibility,' Says Bret Easton Ellis: 'There's a Liberal Mustiness to This Movie'|url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/one-battle-after-another-liberal-critics-bret-easton-ellis-1236545512/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|url-access=subscription |access-date=August 6, 2026}}</ref> Several right-wing commentators, such as [[Ben Shapiro]] or film critic [[Armond White]], criticized ''One Battle'' for being a "left-wing" movie "made for left-wing elites sitting in their left-wing bubble."<ref>{{cite news |last=Gleiberman|first=Owen |author-link=Owen Gleiberman |date=October 19, 2025 |title=No, ''One Battle After Another'' Is Not a 'Left-Wing' Movie |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/columns/no-one-battle-after-another-is-not-a-left-wing-film-1236556461/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|url-access=subscription |access-date=August 6, 2026}}</ref>

During a post-screening panel discussion with Anderson, fellow filmmaker and moderator [[Steven Spielberg]] highly praised the film, calling it "insane" and "really incredible", adding, "This is such a concoction of things that are so bizarre and at the same time so relevant, that I think have become increasingly more relevant than perhaps even when [Anderson] finished the screenplay, and assembled [the] cast and crew, and began production."<ref name="Spielberg"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_lJZ6wKe6dA&t=135s |title='One Battle After Another' with Paul Thomas Producer [[Sara Murphy (film producer)|Sara Murphy]] said she hoped the film's reception among audiences and critics would encourage more studios to invest in "risky" projects similar to it, adding, "Original films are not usually done at this level [of] a big, good-time movie."<ref name="Timeliness"/>

===Critical analysis===
According to Jesse Hassenger of ''The Guardian'', the "film has irked some on the right and galvanized others on the left". Hassenger added that some on the right accused the film for being "an [[apologia]] for radical [[left-wing terrorism]]".<ref>{{cite news |last=Hassenger |first=Jesse |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/sep/30/one-battle-after-another-paul-thomas-anderson |title=The Revolution Will Be in VistaVision: What Are the Politics of 'One Battle After Another'? |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=September 30, 2025 |access-date=December 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930220428/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/sep/30/one-battle-after-another-paul-thomas-anderson |archive-date=September 30, 2025 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Conservatives">{{cite magazine |last=Hibberd |first=James |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/one-battle-after-another-conservative-reactions-1236394128/ |title=Conservatives Take Aim at 'One Battle After Another': 'Year's Most Irresponsible Movie' |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=October 7, 2025 |access-date=October 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007144731/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/one-battle-after-another-conservative-reactions-1236394128/ |archive-date=October 7, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Left-Wing">{{cite magazine |last=Gleiberman |first=Owen |author-link=Owen Gleiberman |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/columns/no-one-battle-after-another-is-not-a-left-wing-film-1236556461/ |title=No, 'One Battle After Another' is Not a 'Left-Wing' Movie |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=October 20, 2025 |access-date=December 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251019175002/https://variety.com/2025/film/columns/no-one-battle-after-another-is-not-a-left-wing-film-1236556461/ |archive-date=October 19, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====Political views and controversies====
''The New York Times''{{'}} [[Michelle Goldberg]] argued it was "an antifascist movie at a fascist moment", a film which she observed "was made in the America that existed before [[Donald Trump]]'s return" to office eight months earlier; Goldberg wondered whether or not "such a forthrightly antifascist film could be produced in Hollywood today".<ref>{{cite news |last=Goldberg |first=Michelle |author-link=Michelle Goldberg |date=September 28, 2025 |title='One Battle After Another', an Antifascist Movie at a Fascist Moment |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/29/opinion/one-battle-after-another-fascism.html |access-date=March 28, 2026 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250929234743/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/29/opinion/one-battle-after-another-fascism.html |archive-date=September 29, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Author, podcaster, and screenwriter [[Bret Easton Ellis]] alleged, "It's kind of shocking to see these kind {{sic}} of accolades for{{snd}}I'm sorry, it's not a very good movie{{snd}}because of its political ideology, and it's so obvious that's what they're responding to [...] Why it's considered a masterpiece, the greatest film of the decade, the greatest film ever made [is] because it really aligns with this kind of leftist sensibility."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Sharf |first=Zack |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/one-battle-after-another-liberal-critics-bret-easton-ellis-1236545512/ |title='One Battle After Another' is a Hit with Critics Because It 'Aligns with a Leftist Sensibility', Says Bret Easton Ellis: 'There's a Liberal Mustiness to This Movie' |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=October 10, 2025 |access-date=March 18, 2026}}</ref> Ellis later added on his podcast allegations that, "You have the left and the entertainment press propping this movie up to such an absurd degree that it felt unnatural."<ref name="Left-Wing"/>

Responding to the political controversies surrounding the film, Gleiberman posited that "part of the power of ''One Battle After Another'' is that it is not, in fact, a left-wing movie, it's important to recognize how that misperception has been fed by a lot of people on the left [...] I think a lot of the attitude of the entertainment media has been to reflexively treat ''One Battle After Another'' as if the film itself were raising a revolutionary fist{{snd}}and as if there were something 'left-wing' about attacking authoritarianism. There is not."<ref name="Left-Wing"/>

====Authoritarian immigration enforcement====

Center]], an ICE facility; the agency is not mentioned directly.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wallace |first=Marlon |date=September 30, 2025 |title=Movie Review{{snd}}One Battle After Another ====Perfidia's character and racial themes====
Ellen E Jones of ''The Guardian'' opined that the film's handling of racial themes "raises questions about how white male directors depict Black women", particularly with regards to Perfidia Beverly Hills, and the ways in which she is [[Sexualization|sexualized]] by two white men (Pat/Bob and Lockjaw, the latter a white supremacist); Bibbiani argued that Perfidia is a [[Sex and the law|sex criminal]].<ref name="TheWrap"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/sep/29/jezebels-race-kink-and-cardi-b-in-one-battle-after-another-black-women-are-still-stereotypes-paul-thomas-anderson |title=Jezebels, race kink and Cardi B: in 'One Battle After Another', Black women are still stereotypes |last=Jones |first=Ellen E |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=September 30, 2025 |access-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-date=September 29, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250929141310/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/sep/29/jezebels-race-kink-and-cardi-b-in-one-battle-after-another-black-women-are-still-stereotypes-paul-thomas-anderson |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |quote=Sadly, it seems{{snd}}with regard to the intersection of race and gender, at least{{snd}}[Anderson]'s bitten off more than he can chew. This begins with the character of Perfidia, who is hyper-sexualised way beyond the normal horniness that firework-lighting in the company of late-era Leonardo DiCaprio might arouse. This is a woman who prioritises getting off over getting away from an imminently exploding bomb.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://asapjournal.com/review/no-rape-involved-racial-fantasies-and-state-violence-in-one-battle-after-another/ |title=No Rape Involved. Racial Fantasies and State Violence in 'One Battle After Another' |last=Noël |first=Fania |publisher=ASAP/Review |date=October 22, 2025 |access-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-date=November 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251114205519/https://asapjournal.com/review/no-rape-involved-racial-fantasies-and-state-violence-in-one-battle-after-another/ |url-status=live |quote=This film has at its center violent politics, armed resistance and sexual enigma [...] The hypersexualization of Perfidia excludes her from the realm of sexual abuse victimhood.}}</ref> ''The New York Times''{{'}} Maya Phillips called Perfidia "the most radical part" of the film, writing, "In one major sense, the film does send a nuanced political message embodied in the brief and mysterious arc of Perfidia Beverly Hills: that the success of a contemporary American political movement is inextricably tied to the sexual freedom and agency of Black women."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/16/movies/one-battle-after-another-black-sexuality.html |title=The Politics of 'One Battle After Another' Are Clear on One Point |last=Phillips |first=Maya |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 16, 2026 |access-date=March 16, 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In November 2025, Taylor rejected these critiques, stating:

{{Blockquote|Is that not what Black women go through? We are [[Race and sexuality#Black women|fetishized]] [...] and we are, unfortunately, the least protected people. Showing what Black women go through, that's a hard reality to accept. And this movie should spark debate, I always knew it would, because sometimes you just got to shake the table.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/teyana-taylor-interview-alls-fair-one-battle-after-another-1236417835/ |title=Teyana Taylor Takes Over |last=O'Connell |first=Mikey |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=November 5, 2025 |access-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-date=January 1, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101201522/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/teyana-taylor-interview-alls-fair-one-battle-after-another-1236417835/ |url-status=live}}</ref>}}

In January 2026, Taylor explained further: "[People feel] like she was overly horny. And I'm like, do you realize the first thing we see of Perfidia is her having a gun to a guy's head, and he calls her 'sweet thing'? Are you{{snd}}are we watching the same film?" She said that Perfidia weaponizes her sexuality against her enemies: "Perfidia kind of dived into the, 'Oh, you think I'm hot? All right, bet. Cool if I get to still do what I'm doing'." Perfidia's decisions, Taylor said, are made in "survival mode":

{{Blockquote|It will never be a moment of judgment, because a lot of her mistakes have come from her being in survival mode, dealing with [[postpartum depression]] and the title of being a strong woman{{snd}}a [[Strong black woman|strong Black woman]]. We don't get the same amount of compassion as everybody else. We don't get the same amount of grace as everybody else. Everybody just assumes we're okay.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/teyana-taylor-golden-globes-breakout-year |title=Teyana Taylor Has Arrived: The Veteran Star on Her Breakout Year |last=Lindsey |first=Underwood |magazine=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |date=January 13, 2026 |access-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116021952/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/teyana-taylor-golden-globes-breakout-year |url-status=live}}</ref>}}

In February 2026, Taylor stated that Perfidia "is so misunderstood, but most importantly, human, and so raw. And she is unapologetically herself", adding:

{{Blockquote|[People] just write her off as like, she's just horny [...] Perfidia became a revolutionary because of the things that she believes in. You see her mom saying Perfidia comes from a long line of revolutionaries. That in itself, to any woman, any person, is also a pressure. So not only is she carrying it on, it is instilled in her, and now it's become a part of her identity.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/teyana-taylor-defends-one-battle-after-another-perfidia-scene-that-hit-hard-11905646 |title=Teyana Taylor is setting the record straight on her 'One Battle After Another' character{{snd}}and reveals the day on set that 'hit hard' |last=Hall |first=Gerrad |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 26, 2026}}</ref>}}

In March 2026, backstage at the [[98th Academy Awards]], Anderson addressed the critiques regarding Perfidia's character:

{{Blockquote|[Perfidia] was so flawed and unfortunately makes decisions that are detrimental to the revolution that she's trying to fight. It's complicated. We always knew that we were trying to make something complicated. We knew that we weren't making something that was heroic and we needed to lean into that. We need to own the fact that this woman was suffering not only from postpartum depression, but she had issues of her own that she hadn't really reconciled with. It's a very dangerous thing, when you start out and want to change the world, but you start to kind of become selfish; you read your own reviews. That was our hero in Perfidia, who becomes an antihero. The point of it is to set up a story of Willa, the next generation. What happens when your parents, who are damaged and have handed quite a difficult history to you{{snd}}how do you manage that?  That's our story. Our story is in Chase [Infiniti] and her reaching, like I talked about in terms of the generational aspect, to try to do better.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/paul-thomas-anderson-racial-criticism-one-battle-another-oscars-1236534115/ |title=Paul Thomas Anderson Addresses Criticism Around Portrayal of Black Women in 'One Battle After Another' Following Oscar Win |last1=Chuba |first1=Kirsten |last2=Fell |first2=Nicole |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=March 15, 2026 |access-date=March 15, 2026}}</ref>}}

101 of the 148 critics who voted had ''One Battle After Another'' somewhere on their Top 10 ballots, while 43 of those 101 mentions were #1 picks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-movies-2025-critics-poll-surveys-performances-1235167619/ |title=2025 Critics Poll: The Best Movies of the Year, According to 148 Critics |last=Blauvelt |first=Christian |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=December 15, 2025 |quote=What's remarkable about such praise for one film is how far-flung the critics who voted in our poll really are: Yes, the majority by far is still from the U.S. or Canada, but six continents are again represented this year{{snd}}even if the number of voters in this survey continues to decline each year as more and more critics leave the industry. |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215160453/https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-movies-2025-critics-poll-surveys-performances-1235167619/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Additionally, ''IndieWire'' surveyed fifty filmmakers' favorite films of the year; twenty listed ''One Battle After Another''. These included [[Fede Álvarez]], [[Olivier Assayas]], [[Clint Bentley]], [[Oliver Laxe]], and [[Michael Mann]]; Laxe called the film "a testament to the excess of our times, on every level".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-movies-2025/ |title=50 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2025 |last=O'Falt |first=Chris |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=December 30, 2025 |access-date=December 30, 2025 |quote=Not surprisingly, filmmakers loved many of the same movies that have dominated critics' top 10 lists: ''One Battle After Another'', ''[[Sinners (2025 film)|Sinners]]'', and ''[[Sentimental Value]]'' being the most frequently mentioned titles. |archive-date=December 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251230201557/https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-movies-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In his list of 2025's 20 best films, ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s David Fear called ''One Battle After Another'' a "thundering, dizzying epic", and "a timeless tale about revolutionaries taking care of their own while getting the next generation to pick up the flag".<ref name="RollingStone">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/best-movies-2025-1235440226/ |title=The 20 Best Movies of 2025 |last=Fear |first=David |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=December 1, 2025 |access-date=December 5, 2025 |archive-date=December 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251204174507/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/best-movies-2025-1235440226/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

''One Battle After Another'' appeared on more critics' annual "best of" lists than any other 2025 film, receiving the most #1 votes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yearendlists.com/visuals/one-battle-after-another-b7ed8ae6-c582-45b2-b7d9-cab891c552cf |title=One Battle After Another |publisher=Year-End Lists |access-date=December 22, 2025 |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226135233/https://www.yearendlists.com/visuals/one-battle-after-another-b7ed8ae6-c582-45b2-b7d9-cab891c552cf |url-status=live}}</ref> The film was included on 735 lists, with 212 ranking it at #1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://criticstop10.com/best-movies-of-2025/ |title=Best Movies of 2025 |publisher=CriticsTop10 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |archive-date=January 29, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129054545/https://criticstop10.com/best-movies-of-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref> It appeared on former [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Barack Obama]]'s annual list of his favorite films of each year; though it was not ranked, ''One Battle After Another'' appeared at the top of the list.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.obama.org/stories/favorites-2025/ |title=Check out President Obama's Favorite Films, Books, and Music of 2025 |publisher=[[Obama Foundation|Obama.org]] |date=December 18, 2025 |access-date=December 18, 2025 |archive-date=December 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251219043920/https://www.obama.org/stories/favorites-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |number=2001752388974121278 |user=BarackObama |last=Obama |first=Barack |title=As 2025 comes to a close, I'm continuing a tradition that I started during my time in the White House: sharing my annual lists of favorite books, movies, and music. I hope you find something new to enjoy{{snd}}and please send any recommendations for me to check out! |date=December 18, 2025 |access-date=December 18, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/lists/obama-favorite-films-2025-books-songs/ |title=Obama's Favorite Films of 2025 include 'Sinners', 'Hamnet' & 'One Battle After Another' with Kendrick Lamar and Drake in Top Songs |last=Gomez |first=Dessi |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=December 18, 2025 |access-date=December 18, 2025 |archive-date=December 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251219192241/https://deadline.com/lists/obama-favorite-films-2025-books-songs/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

mockery and scorn, is a courageous one. |archive-date=January 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116101800/https://www.slashfilm.com/2075922/best-2025-movie-villains-ranked/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2025, ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]''{{'}}s William Smith ranked ''One Battle After Another'' 9th on his list of the "10 Greatest Movie Masterpieces of the Last 10 Years", calling it one of "the most imminent" and "entertaining" films of the year, and adding that its "righteous indignation" and "bold politics" feel "particularly pointed and appropriate for the current state of America".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/best-movie-masterpieces-last-10-years-ranked/ |title=10 Greatest Movie Masterpieces of the Last 10 Years, Ranked |last=Smith |first=William |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=December 11, 2025 |access-date=December 28, 2025 |archive-date=January 5, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105053330/https://collider.com/best-movie-masterpieces-last-10-years-ranked/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Collider''{{'}}s Diego Pineda Pacheco ranked the film 8th on his list of the "10 Greatest Movie Masterpieces of the 21st Century", writing, "[Anderson] has been delivering masterpiece after masterpiece since the '90s, but this one truly does feel like the epitome of his career, an artistic achievement unlike any other he's made before ... [the film] is full of fascinating characters and exceptional performers, making it an enthralling dramedy packed with exquisite creative choices."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/best-movie-masterpieces-21st-century-ranked/ |title=10 Greatest Movie Masterpieces of the 21st Century, Ranked |last=Pacheco |first=Diego Pineda |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=December 5, 2025 |access-date=January 1, 2026 |quote=[Anderson] has been delivering masterpiece after masterpiece since the '90s, but this one truly does feel like the epitome of his career, an artistic achievement unlike any other he's made before. |archive-date=December 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251231210746/https://collider.com/best-movie-masterpieces-21st-century-ranked/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2026, ''Collider'' ranked ''One Battle After Another'' as the best film of 2025 in their list of "The Greatest Movie of Every Year of the 21st Century (So Far)", writing that it is "a comedic epic of sorts" and "moves at a mean pace and never drags", adding, "The tension is never undermined by the comedy, and the comedy never clashes with the parts of the film that are meant to be a bit more serious. It's incredibly well-balanced for something so grand and ambitious, and it seems likely that it'll continue to remain entertaining, relevant, and distinctive as the years march on further."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/best-movies-21st-century-every-year-so-far/ |title=The Greatest Movie of Every Year of the 21st Century (So Far) |last=Urquhart |first=Jeremy |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=February 23, 2026 |access-date=February 24, 2026 |archive-date=February 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260224002045/https://collider.com/best-movies-21st-century-every-year-so-far/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Accolades===
{{Main|List of accolades received by One Battle After Another|l1=List of accolades received by ''One Battle After Another''}}
At the [[31st Critics' Choice Awards]], ''One Battle After Another'' won three awards, including [[Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for Anderson.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/critics-choice-awards-winners-2026-list-1236661448/ |title=Critics Choice Awards: 'One Battle After Another' Wins Best Picture as Paul Thomas Anderson Takes Best Director; Chalamet & Buckley Win Top Acting Prizes; 'Sinners' & 'Frankenstein' Lead with 4 Each |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=January 4, 2026 |access-date=January 5, 2026 |archive-date=January 5, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105012515/https://deadline.com/2026/01/critics-choice-awards-winners-2026-list-1236661448/ |url-status=live}}</ref> It was also nominated for nine awards at the [[83rd Golden Globes]], receiving the most nominations of any film that year; del Toro, DiCaprio, Infiniti, Penn, and Taylor all received nominations for their performances. Ultimately, the film won four Golden Globes: [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy]], [[Golden Globe Award for Best Director|Best Director]], [[Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress – Motion Picture|Best Supporting Actress – Motion Picture]] (Taylor), and [[Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay|Best Screenplay]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/awards/golden-globes-2026-nominations-one-battle-after-another-1236601172/ |title=Golden Globes 2026 Nominations: 'One Battle After Another' Tops Films with Nine Nods, 'White Lotus' Leads TV with Six |last1=Lang |first1=Brent |last2=Moreau |first2=Jordan |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=December 8, 2025 |access-date=December 18, 2025 |archive-date=December 8, 2025 2026 Golden Globes |last1=Paul |first1=Larisha |last2=Mier |first2=Tomás |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=January 11, 2026 |access-date=January 11, 2026 |archive-date=January 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112082758/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/one-battle-after-another-best-picture-2026-golden-globes-1235495925/ [[98th Academy Awards]], the film received thirteen nominations, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]] and four acting nominations (for del Toro, DiCaprio, Penn, and Taylor), the second-most of any film that year.<ref>{{cite web (Somner,{{efn|Adam Somner became the second producer, following [[Sam Zimbalist]] (for 1959's ''[[Ben-Hur (1959 film)|Ben-Hur]]''), to win [[List of posthumous Academy Award winners and
